results.title: Enhancing social life cycle assessment through stakeholder engagement: Development of a new cellulose-based material - ScienceDirect
results.content: Many studies lack robust methodologies for context-specific approaches on Social Life Cycle Assessment (S-LCA), particularly regarding the selection of meaningful social indicators, systematic stakeholder involvement, and integration of results into a coherent assessment framework. However, many studies primarily focus on the environmental or economic impacts of products or supply chains (Benoit-Norris et al., 2012; Cadena et al., 2019), leading to differences in the maturity of methodologies and tools within a life cycle framework for the three dimensions of sustainability. S-LCA is a methodological approach that provides a comprehensive and systematic understanding of a system (e.g., product or service) negative and positive social impacts throughout its life cycle, from raw material extraction to final disposal (Benoît et al., 2010). Beyond its methodological consolidation, the UNEP/SETAC approach was selected in this study due to its epistemological compatibility with the objectives of conducting a context-specific, stakeholder-centred social assessment. Many studies still lack integrated approaches that connect stakeholder engagement, indicator selection, and the evaluation of social risks and benefits in a coherent and replicable way (Petti et al., 2018; Tokede and Traverso, 2020). To address these challenges, this study proposes an enhanced multi-methodological framework for S-LCA that strengthens stakeholder integration and improves the evaluation of social risks and benefits throughout the value chain, enabling a context-specific assessment. The framework builds upon existing guidelines and incorporates participatory methods, qualitative and semi-quantitative tools, and the Stakeholder Theory to offer a more holistic and structured approach to social impact assessment. Enhanced assessment of social indicators – A robust methodology for selecting, validating, and evaluating social impact indicators, considering both risks and benefits. The case study demonstrates how the multi-methodological approach enhances stakeholder engagement, data collection, and social impact assessment, reinforcing the framework's relevance for future sustainability applications. The research framework proposed in this article builds upon the UNEP/SETAC guidelines for S-LCA, providing a structured and systematic approach for evaluating social impacts throughout the life cycle of the analyzed system (UNEP, 2020). ### Social life cycle assessment methodology for evaluating production process design: biorefinery case study. ### Modeling social life cycle assessment framework for an electronic screen product – A case study of an integrated desktop computer.
